obernants.approximation_semantics: Conditional mathematical relation with finite checks; no universal proof.
obernants.assumptions: Standard Rust execution, sufficient allocation, independently checked oracle within stated bounds.
obernants.domain: Finite allocated adjacency vectors and typed result observations, ordinary terminating Rust execution.
obernants.operator: Let X be allocated finite ordered adjacency vectors and usize right-partition sizes, and Y the typed Result<Vec<Option<usize>>,BipartiteMatchingError> observation space, excluding allocation failure and nontermination. Define R subset X times Y by first-invalid-edge validation followed by the exact ordered FIFO augmenting traversal in Forward, not by arbitrary maximum matching. Set U=X times Y and behavior_complement=U minus R. It includes every valid maximum differing from that deterministic selected vector, as well as invalid, infeasible and submaximum observations. Finite negative fixtures check selected memberships only.

obernants.operator: For output mate vector m, compatible inputs have L=len(m), R greater than every present mate, contain every selected edge and have matching number equal to count(Some). Exact compatibility additionally requires the stated FIFO/adjacency traversal to select m. Different edge sets and duplicate multiplicities can fit one result; unique graph recovery is not claimed. InvalidEdge restricts inputs to the reported first invalid endpoint and all earlier endpoints valid.

obernants.operator: Adding duplicate occurrences preserves maximum cardinality and feasibility. Reordering adjacency preserves optimum size but can change chosen mates. A long alternating chain requires reassignment of existing mates; simple greedy free-neighbor selection does not satisfy the contract.

obernants.approximation_semantics: Exact conditional mathematical relation with bounded Rust correspondence; no universal verification.
obernants.assumptions: Original deterministic Rust; graph endpoint validation; sufficient allocation. Specialized domains are stated in each relation.
obernants.domain: Validated finite adjacency vectors; exact representable arithmetic; sufficient allocation.
obernants.observation_scope: Successful outputs and declared transformed inputs; errors only where explicitly stated.
obernants.operator: For a valid graph and feasible matching M, orient unmatched edges left-to-right and matched edges right-to-left. M is maximum iff no residual path connects a free left vertex to a free right vertex. Feasibility requires original-edge membership and distinct matched right endpoints. The production result is checked over all 512 simple 3-by-3 graphs. Duplicates do not change the cardinality relation.

obernants.operator: From all free left vertices let Z_L,Z_R be alternating residual reachability. For a maximum matching, C=(L minus Z_L) union Z_R covers every edge and |C|=|M|. Thus any matching is at most |C| and returned M attains that bound; this is an independent certificate rather than a second augmenting solver. The 512-graph test checks feasibility, absence of a reached free right, every edge covered and equality of cardinalities. The empty cover is outside the cover relation whenever an edge exists.

obernants.operator: For a validated graph G and one added valid edge e, nu(G)<=nu(G+e)<=nu(G)+1. The lower bound retains any old matching; deleting e from a new maximum proves the upper bound. Exact selected mates need not be preserved. All 512 simple 3-by-3 graphs times nine edge insertions yield 4608 comparisons, including already-present edges.

obernants.operator: Transpose a valid L-by-R graph to R-by-L while preserving edges. Swapping endpoints bijects matchings and therefore preserves maximum cardinality. The deterministic output vector is not an invariant: its length and left order change and tie selection may change. Tests check cardinality for 512 square graphs, and a two-row permutation explicitly rejects vector identity. This finite square fixture does not exhaust rectangular graphs.

obernants.operator: For any feasible output vector M of length L with distinct Some(r)<R, construct G_M by giving row l only its selected r, or no edges for None. Production returns exactly M because each present edge has a distinct right endpoint. Repeating that sole edge also returns M, showing nonunique antecedents whenever M is nonempty. This is a sound subset of the deterministic output preimage. It does not imply every graph where M is maximum yields M. Tests reconstruct outputs from 512 graphs and reject both duplicate-right output and a different maximum matching for an ordered complete 2-by-2 graph.
